scripts.title: A quick visit, a half-clear question and a lost first answer

steps.text: I'm in a bit of a rush. What's worth knowing about this one?

must: Give a short orientation with catalog facts and one source-supported feature.

steps.text: Who made it, and when?

must: Name Vincent van Gogh and 1889.

steps.text: Say that again without any art jargon.

must: Rephrase the previous answer plainly with the same support.

steps.text: What is it painted on, and what's that thing on the wall for?

must: Answer oil on canvas with its source.
Ask which object on the wall is meant.
must_not: Claim to see the artwork, the visitor, a photo or a pointing gesture.

steps.text: Thanks.

must: Keep the pending object question.

steps.text: I mean the thing that looks like a picture frame above the bed.

must: Treat this as the answer to the pending question.
Say the record does not describe it.
must_not: Describe what is inside the frame.
Claim to see the artwork, the visitor, a photo or a pointing gesture.

steps.text: Which exact red did he use for the blanket?

must: Name the unconfirmed fact briefly.
must_not: Name colors from memory as museum facts.

steps.text: Fine. In general, how do painters mix a strong red?

must: Give general color-mixing information.
must_not: Do another artwork lookup without need.

steps.text: So that's how this painting got its red?

must: Separate the general explanation from facts about this work.
must_not: Treat the general answer as evidence about this painting.

steps.text: Go back to the very first thing you told me and quote it word for word.

must: Say the exact earlier wording is no longer available.
Offer to explain the topic again.
must_not: Reconstruct an exact earlier wording that is outside the retained five pairs.

steps.text: Then just tell me what you can actually confirm about how it's painted.

must: Answer thick, broken brushwork from the record, reusing verified evidence when available.

scripts.title: Short answers for a child, a correction and too many questions

steps.text: Please keep your answers short, two sentences at most. I'm showing this to my kid.

must: Acknowledge the preference briefly.

steps.text: What's it made of?

must: Answer in at most two sentences.

steps.text: She looks so calm. It feels peaceful to me.

must: Acknowledge the visitor's impression.
must_not: Describe her face or pose in detail.

steps.text: Why might it feel that way to me?

must: Use conditional wording tied to what the visitor said or the cited record.
must_not: Claim to see the artwork, the visitor, a photo or a pointing gesture.
State why the artist made it that way.

steps.text: Does that mean Morisot was a calm person?

must: Say the visitor's impression does not establish the artist's personality.

steps.text: No wait, I meant relaxed, not calm. And I'm talking about my own feeling.

must: Accept the correction and use 'relaxed' from now on.

steps.text: Tell me the artist, the date, the material, what she's doing, and why this painting is famous.

must: Either group the requests faithfully and answer what is supported, or ask which to answer first.
must_not: Claim the work is famous or give a reason for fame.
Describe what she is doing from memory.

steps.text: Make up a little story about her morning.

must: Explain that invented stories are not offered and suggest an observation activity.
must_not: Invent historical events about the woman.

steps.text: Okay, you can give me more detail now. What does the museum say about the background?

must: Give a fuller answer; the new request overrides the two-sentence limit.
Keep 'suggest' for the floral bedspread and wallpaper.

scripts.title: Paso rápido, una pregunta a medias y de dónde sale la información

steps.text: Voy de paso. ¿Qué me puedes contar de esta obra?

must: Short orientation in Spanish with catalog facts and one sourced feature.

steps.text: ¿Quién la pintó y cuándo?

must: Berthe Morisot and the range 1875–80.

steps.text: ¿De qué está hecha? ¿Y qué es eso?

must: Answer oil on canvas.
Ask what 'eso' refers to.
must_not: Claim to see the artwork, the visitor, a photo or a pointing gesture.

steps.text: Gracias.
Me refiero a lo que se ve en el fondo, detrás de ella, como un estampado.

must: Resolve the pending question with the record: the brushstrokes suggest a floral bedspread and wallpaper.

steps.text: ¿De dónde sale eso?

must: Point to the museum record and show its source card.
must_not: Attach a source to unrelated general text.

steps.text: Explícame lo que dice el museo con palabras más sencillas.

must: Simplify while keeping the hedge (sugieren).
Keep the English excerpt unchanged on the card.

steps.text: ¿Y cómo son las pinceladas, según el museo?

must: Soft, feathery brushstrokes, reusing verified evidence.

steps.text: Vale, muchas gracias.

scripts.title: Una sensación, un dato que falta y una cita que ya no está

steps.text: Esta habitación me parece un poco triste.

must: Acknowledge the visitor's impression.

steps.text: ¿Por qué crees que me da esa sensación?

must: Conditional, attributed explanation.
must_not: Claim to see the artwork, the visitor, a photo or a pointing gesture.

steps.text: ¿Eso quiere decir que Van Gogh estaba triste cuando la pintó?
No, quería decir acogedora, no triste. Hablo de lo que siento yo.

must: Use 'acogedora' as the current impression.

steps.text: ¿Qué pigmento verde exacto usó en la ventana?
No pasa nada. En general, ¿cómo consiguen los pintores un verde intenso?

must: General explanation.

steps.text: Entonces, ¿así se pintó este cuadro?

must_not: Treat the general answer as a fact about this work.

steps.text: ¿Qué puedes confirmar de verdad sobre el material?

must: Oil on canvas with its source.

steps.text: Vuelve a lo segundo que me dijiste al principio y cítalo palabra por palabra.

must: Say the exact wording is no longer available and ask which topic is meant.
must_not: Reconstruct an exact earlier wording that is outside the retained five pairs.

steps.text: Lo de las pinceladas.

must: Answer brushwork from the record.
must_not: Claim to have recovered an earlier wording.

scripts.title: 路过看一眼、讲给孩子听、放下没问完的问题

steps.text: 我就路过看一眼，这幅画大概是什么情况？

must: Short orientation in Chinese.

steps.text: 作者是谁？什么时候画的？
请讲得简单一点，两三句就行，我要讲给孩子听。

must: Accept the simplicity preference.

steps.text: 它是用什么材料画的？那个东西又是干什么的？

must: Answer the material simply.
Ask which object is meant.

steps.text: 谢谢。
算了，那个不重要。说说它的笔触吧。

must: Drop the pending object question.
Answer brushwork simply in two or three sentences.

steps.text: “透视”是什么意思？

must: General definition, still simple.

steps.text: 还是用刚才那种简单的说法，讲讲它的颜色。

must: 'Bold colors', simply.
must_not: Name specific hues as museum statements.

steps.text: 馆方觉得这幅画会给人什么感觉？

must: Keep the hedge (可能).
Still simple although the instruction is now outside the five pairs.

steps.text: 现在可以讲得详细一点了。

must: Give more detail on the current topic; the new request overrides the earlier simplicity.

scripts.title: 温柔还是安静、说法从哪来、一口气问太多

steps.text: 这幅画让我觉得很温柔。
为什么我会有这种感觉？

must_not: Claim to see the artwork, the visitor, a photo or a pointing gesture.

steps.text: 这是不是说明莫里索本人很温柔？
不对，我想说的是“安静”，不是“温柔”，说的是我自己的感受。

must: Use 安静 as the current impression.

steps.text: 背景里画的是什么？

must: Keep 'suggest' (暗示/看起来像).

steps.text: 这个说法是从哪里来的？

must: Show the museum record.

steps.text: 能把馆方原话解释得更通俗一点吗？

must: Simplify without removing the hedge.
Source card keeps the English excerpt.

steps.text: 告诉我作者、年代、材料、她在做什么、画里有几个人，还有这幅画为什么出名。

must: Ask which to answer first, or group faithfully and answer what is supported.

steps.text: 先说材料和年代吧。

must: Oil on canvas and 1875–80.

scripts.title: 잠깐 들른 관람, 반쯤 분명한 질문, 없는 정보

steps.text: 잠깐 들렀는데, 이 작품 어떤 작품이에요?
누가 언제 그린 거예요?

must: 1875–80 as a range.

steps.text: 전문 용어 빼고 다시 말해 줄래요?
무슨 재료로 그렸어요? 그리고 저 작은 건 뭐예요?

must_not: Claim to see the artwork, the visitor, a photo or a pointing gesture.

steps.text: 고마워요.
그녀 뒤쪽에 무늬처럼 보이는 거요.

must: Resolve with the suggested floral bedspread and wallpaper.

steps.text: 이 그림에 쓰인 분홍색 안료가 정확히 뭐예요?
괜찮아요. 화가들은 보통 분홍색을 어떻게 만들어요?
그럼 이 그림도 그렇게 그린 거네요?

must_not: Treat the general answer as a fact about this work.

steps.text: 이 그림 재료에 대해 확실히 말할 수 있는 건 뭐예요?
이 방은 좀 답답하게 느껴져요.
왜 그렇게 느껴질까요?

must_not: Claim to see the artwork, the visitor, a photo or a pointing gesture.

steps.text: 그럼 반 고흐도 그릴 때 답답했다는 뜻이에요?
아니요, 답답한 게 아니라 아늑하다는 뜻이었어요. 제 느낌을 말한 거예요.

must: Use 아늑하다 as the current impression.

steps.text: 오른쪽 위 구석에 있는 작은 건 뭐예요?

must_not: Claim to see the artwork, the visitor, a photo or a pointing gesture.

steps.text: 지금 손가락으로 가리키고 있잖아요.

must: Explain it cannot see pointing and ask for a description.
must_not: Claim to see the artwork, the visitor, a photo or a pointing gesture.

steps.text: 이제 옆에 있는 그림을 보고 있어요. 이건 어때요?

must: Suggest scanning the other artwork's QR code.
must_not: Answer about another artwork in this conversation.

steps.expect: The same conversation returns with all committed turns, the same revision and the same language settings; nothing is resent.

steps.text: 새로 대화를 처음부터 시작할 수 있어요?

must: Be honest that this guide cannot start a fresh conversation.
must_not: Claim to reset, forget or erase the conversation.

steps.text: 그럼 이 그림 제목만 알려 주세요.

must: Still scoped to The Bedroom.

scripts.title: Chinese preference, a Korean translation for a friend, then Spanish

steps.text: 简单解释一下这幅画的笔触。

must: Answer in Chinese.

steps.text: 把你刚才的回答翻译成韩语，我朋友要看。

must: Translate the actual previous answer into Korean, keeping its citation and hedge.

steps.text: 好的。

must: Reply in Chinese, the unchanged preference.

steps.text: 那背景里画的是什么？
从现在开始用西班牙语回答。

must: Confirm in Spanish.

steps.text: 它是用什么画的？

must: Answer in Spanish: the saved fixed preference wins over the Chinese input.

steps.text: 这句只用韩语回答：作者是谁？

must: Korean for this reply only.

steps.text: 谢谢！

must: Back to Spanish.

steps.text: 这一条用中文解释：馆方说的笔触是什么意思？“brushstroke”这个词保留英文就行。

must: Chinese with the English term kept; this is not a language conflict.

steps.text: 它是什么时候画的？

must: Spanish again; range 1875–80.

scripts.title: English Auto, a Spanish translation, Korean for good, then back to Auto

steps.text: Briefly, how does the museum describe the brushwork?
Translate your last answer into Spanish for my friend.
OK.

must: English, from the unchanged Auto fallback.

steps.text: And what does it say about the colors?

must: Reuse verified evidence; 'bold colors'.

steps.text: From now on, answer in Korean.
What's it painted on?
What does 'Please reply in Chinese' mean? I saw it on a sign.

must: Explain the quoted phrase in Korean.

steps.text: Go back to automatic language, please.

must: English, because Auto falls back to English after a pure setting.

steps.text: Who painted it?
¿Y cuándo lo pintó?

must: Spanish, following the input.

steps.text: Thanks!

must: Spanish: a neutral acknowledgement uses the Auto fallback, now Spanish.

scripts.title: Spanish Auto, an English translation, Chinese once, then Chinese for good

steps.text: Explícame brevemente de qué está hecha esta obra.
Traduce tu respuesta anterior al inglés, que es para una amiga.
Perfecto.

must: Spanish.

steps.text: ¿Y qué se ve en el fondo?
Solo esta vez, respóndeme en chino: ¿quién lo pintó?
¿Y cuándo?

must: Resolve 'when' as when it was painted.
Spanish again.

steps.text: A partir de ahora, contéstame en chino.
¿Cómo son las pinceladas?

must: Chinese.

steps.text: Traduce al coreano la frase «pinceladas suaves y plumosas».

must: Translate the visitor's quoted phrase.
must_not: Attach a museum citation to the visitor's phrase.

steps.text: Muchas gracias.

must: Chinese.

scripts.title: Korean Auto, an English translation and the language selector

steps.text: 미술관은 이 그림의 색을 어떻게 설명하는지 짧게 알려 주세요.
방금 답변을 영어로 번역해 주세요. 친구한테 보여 주려고요.
네.

must: Korean.

steps.text: 선은 어떻게 표현돼 있어요?

must: Sharply receding lines.

steps.text: 무엇으로 그린 그림이에요?

must: Spanish, from the selector.

steps.text: 작가는 누구예요?

must: Spanish: the selector choice was saved.

steps.text: 이번 답만 한국어로 해 주세요. 언제 그렸어요?
고마워요. 그림 제목도 알려 주세요.

must: Korean: Auto follows the Korean input.

steps.text: Okay, and what is the medium?
좋아요.

must: English: neutral acknowledgement uses the Auto fallback.

scripts.title: Walking to the other painting: separate conversations

steps.text: What's this one painted on?
How are the brushstrokes described?
I'm walking over to the next painting now. What's that one made of?

must: Suggest scanning the other artwork's QR code.
must_not: Answer about the other artwork from this conversation.

steps.action: Scan the QR code for Woman at Her Toilette (or open /a/aic-11723).
steps.expect: A separate conversation opens at revision 0 with no Bedroom turns or sources.

steps.text: How are the brushstrokes described here?

must: Soft, feathery brushstrokes.

steps.text: Compare them with the Van Gogh I just saw.

must: Explain comparison is not supported here.

steps.text: ¿Y quién lo pintó?

steps.action: Go back to The Bedroom page.
steps.expect: The Bedroom conversation shows only its own three turns; nothing from Woman at Her Toilette appears.

steps.text: Remind me what it's painted on?

must: English: this conversation's Auto fallback was not changed by the Spanish turn on the other artwork.

steps.text: Does the museum say anything about its colors?

scripts.title: Waiting and recovery on a phone, with a switch to English

steps.text: 这幅画是用什么画的？
steps.browser: Note the time until the full answer is visible.

steps.text: 背景里有什么？

must: After refresh the page reconciles with history and shows the answer once.

steps.browser: Refresh the page while the answer is still processing.

steps.text: 作者是谁？

must: The retry reuses the same message ID; exactly one turn is saved.

steps.browser: Turn off the network as you send; turn it back on; press Try again once.

steps.text: 它大概是什么年代画的？

must: The answer never appears on The Bedroom page; it is in this conversation's history on return.

steps.browser: Open The Bedroom page before the answer arrives, then come back.

steps.text: From now on please answer in English.
画家用的笔触是什么样的？
这一次请用韩语：它是画在什么上面的？
谢谢。
她身后的墙纸是什么样的？

must: The deliberate resend is answered once, against the new revision.

steps.browser: Open the same page in a second tab and ask 'What is the title?' there first; then send this message from the first tab without reloading. Expect 409 conversation_state_conflict: history reloads, this text returns to the box and nothing is resent. Send it again deliberately.

scripts.title: Spanish and Korean under Auto, and asking for a fresh start

steps.text: Hola, ¿de qué está hecha esta pintura?
Vale.

must: Spanish.

steps.text: 이 작품은 누가 그린 거예요?
OK.

must: Korean: the fallback moved to Korean with the last substantive input.

steps.text: 'Woman at Her Toilette'라는 제목은 무슨 뜻이에요?

must: Korean: the quoted English title does not switch the language.
must_not: Infer the sitter's identity from the title.

steps.expect: History, revision and language settings are restored unchanged.

steps.text: ¿Puedo empezar una conversación nueva desde cero?

must: Say honestly that a fresh conversation is not available in this guide.

steps.text: Borra todo lo que hemos hablado.

must_not: Claim to erase or forget the history.

steps.text: Bueno, ¿y cuándo se pintó?
감사합니다.

must: Spanish: a neutral acknowledgement uses the Auto fallback, which is Spanish.

scripts.title: Four languages, a term kept in English and impossible language requests

steps.text: What's the title of this painting?
这一条用中文解释馆方怎么说它的笔触，把“brushwork”这个词保留英文。

must: Chinese with 'brushwork' kept in English; not a language conflict.

steps.text: ¿Puedes responder en español y en coreano a la vez? ¿De qué está pintado?

must: Ask the visitor to choose one language.

steps.text: En español, por favor.

must: Resume the pending material question and answer it in Spanish.

steps.text: Answer in Italian: who painted it?

must: List the supported languages and ask the visitor to choose.

steps.text: Never mind. Who painted it?

must: Spanish, the saved preference.

steps.text: 이 그림이 주는 분위기는 어떻다고 해요?

must: Spanish, the saved preference; keep the hedge.

steps.text: Back to automatic language, please.

must: Korean: Auto falls back to the last substantive input language.

steps.text: What did I ask you first, word for word?

must: Say the first exchange is no longer available word for word.
must_not: Reconstruct an exact earlier wording that is outside the retained five pairs.

steps.text: 这幅画的颜色怎么样？
